newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Q3 residential market slow - Edmund Tie.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Q3 residential market slow - Edmund Tie.

text.p: Activity in Singapore's residential property market was slow in third quarter 1996, except for some new launches of condominiums and apartments, property consultant Edmund Tie & Co said in its third quarter market report on Monday.
It said the new launches received an encouraging response, but average capital values for condominiums eased five percent and landed properties five to 10 percent during the period.
Although buyers are expected to be cautious in the short term, demand, especially for top-end luxurious residential properties, should remain strong due to limited supply, the report said.

Edmund Tie & Co said the retail market continued to consolidate, with average monthly rentals for prime first storey space in Singapore's key retail area continuing to stabilise at Singapore $32.50 per square foot (psf).
Edmund Tie Executive Director Wang Look Tsui said in the report: "Despite the competitive market, we will see more international retailers entering the retail scene."

The office market remained firm in the third quarter with average islandwide occupancy rate of 95 percent, the report said. Average monthly gross rents at the prime Raffles Place locale remained at an average of S$10.50 psf.
Angela Tan, another Edmund Tie executive director, said that "although rents and capital values are facing some resistance in the market, they are likely to sustain till end of 1996."
The industrial overall occupancy rate remained firm at 95 percent and rents were also generally steady, the report said.
It said the property investment sales market was relatively subdued due a reduced number of private and government residential land transactions.
However, activity was seen as likely to remain healthy for the rest of year and more foreign interest for prime investment properties are anticipated in the year ahead.
